_note: The parameter catalogue for this corpus: every number a statute did not state, with its unit (the corpus's own units are accepted and scaled by the decoder), the convention its value comes from and its source. It starts empty: the plan decides which parameters exist and proposes each with a provisional value, and the harness enters the proposal here marked `proposed` (run, iteration, node) until the operator reviews it by removing the marker or changing the value; the doctor lists every unreviewed proposal. The operator-authored list this file carried before any law was planned is kept, out of the pipeline's path, under readings/legacy/. Figures the law states are literals on the rule's span, never entries here.

params.name: p.backing_window
params.convention: The length of the window behind over which rearward travel is recognized as backing rather than as sampling noise or a momentary roll-back on a grade, and the window over which the heading swing of a corner is integrated. It bounds the recognition of the act, not how far a vehicle may reverse.
params.source: manoeuvre-recognition windows over trajectory datasets sampled at their usual rate.

params.name: p.speed_zero_tolerance
params.convention: The speed at or below which a tracked body's displacement between observations is indistinguishable from standing on the source's own position resolution; here it is the floor below which rearward travel counts as no motion at all.
params.source: position-noise and resting-speed figures of road-user tracking datasets and perception benchmarks.

params.name: p.corner_heading_change
params.convention: The heading swing through which a body passes in going from one street into an intersecting one. DEF-NRS-484A-105 has the two highways “join one another at, or approximately at, right angles”, and the bound is set inside that angle so that skewed junctions and a reversing path that is still completing its swing are covered, while a vehicle reversing straight back is not.
params.source: turning-path templates for intersection design (passenger-car turning envelopes).

params.name: p.corner_reach
params.convention: The ground distance from the intersection region within which a reversing turn counts as taken around that junction's corner, so that a swing made far down the block is not. It is a corner-geometry figure, the reach of the turning envelope off the junction.
params.source: turning-path templates for intersection design: corner radii and turning-envelope offsets.

params.name: p.turn_window
params.convention: The length of the window behind over which a turning's heading change is integrated: the time an ordinary vehicle takes to carry a turn at a junction, or a reversal of direction, from the start of the swing to its end, long enough to carry a reversal made in more than one movement as DEF-NRS-484B-077 requires. It bounds the observation of the manoeuvre and is not a judgement of how long a turn may take.
params.source: turning-manoeuvre durations at low speed reported in junction design guidance

params.name: p.turn_reversal_tolerance
params.convention: The angle by which an integrated heading change may fall short of a half turn and still be read as a turning “so as to proceed in the opposite direction”: the spread of headings a way holds between its two directions, which its bends and its camber give a body that has turned about. It is an observer's tolerance on an absolute of the definition, not a judgement of how complete a turn must be.
params.source: lane alignment and heading tolerances in road geometry and map matching

params.name: p.yaw_rate_floor
params.convention: The rate of change of heading at or above which a tracked body counts as turning rather than holding its heading: the resolution of the source's yaw channel, below which a reading is indistinguishable from tracking noise. It names only the source's resolution and no degree of manoeuvre.
params.source: yaw-rate noise floors of vehicle inertial units and of heading estimates on tracked road users

params.name: p.yellow_phase_window
params.convention: The window behind an observation within which a steady yellow is sought when the head shows red: the length of the yellow change interval a signal is timed with, so that a red displayed within it is the red the yellow of this paragraph warned of, and a red displayed later belongs to a phase of its own. The interval is set from the approach speed and the driver's reaction and braking, and the value is taken at the upper end of the range ordinary signal timing uses.
params.source: ITE Traffic Engineering Handbook and the MUTCD guidance on yellow change intervals.

params.name: p.turn_intent_window
params.convention: The window ahead within which the turn a road user is intending must be made for the intention to be read from the act: the time between the point at which a driver has committed to a turn at a junction and the turning itself, over an ordinary approach at junction speeds.
params.source: Driver-behaviour studies of turn preparation and signalling distance on junction approaches (ITE and NCHRP intersection-design literature).

params.name: p.approach_lookback_window
params.convention: The window behind within which the lane by which a road user reached a junction is sought: the time an ordinary approach to a junction takes from the lane being settled to the entry, at urban approach speeds.
params.source: Junction approach timing in the ITE Traffic Engineering Handbook.

params.name: p.curve_radius_floor
params.convention: The radius of the flattest horizontal alignment a road map's geometry and a fitted trajectory still tell from a tangent, with which the curvature read at a road user's position is compared by its reciprocal. The parameter names the source's resolution only, so that the condition is the presence of a bend and not a bend of some stated sharpness.
params.source: Curvature estimation tolerances of road centreline geometry and map-matched trajectories.

params.name: p.crest_reach
params.convention: The ground distance from a crest region within which a road user is upon the approach to or near that crest: the length of approach over which the crest cuts short a driver's view of the road beyond, taken as the stopping sight distance a rural two-lane highway of ordinary design speed is laid out for, which is the length the crest's vertical curve is designed from.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping sight distance and crest vertical curve design.

_fields.aggregates: optional operator overrides only: word, classes (ru.* ids or other words). The run derives every aggregate the laws use from the corpus definitions (results/<run>/reading.json, for review); an operator entry here takes precedence over the derived one.
